body:
# the contributor audit: joint cover hinge and midpoint source bound

The complete cover-hinge results and the all-dimensional three-quarter
source bound pass this audit. They do not prove the general OC inequality.

## 1. Continuously normalized full-cover potential

Source: `candidate de8d1a3251731edd`.

The lower threshold bound follows directly from the bounded hinge
integral and each positive fiber's mass. Finite threshold coordinates
have closed linear restriction image. For threshold saturation the
correct kernel sequence is e_k-v-R_I(e_k|I-v|I); this explicit subtraction
was added after this audit. Its infinite coordinates still tend to positive
infinity, so one finite kernel vector saturates all of them. Uniform
hinge convergence, null continuous hyperplanes, and finite cap count
give respectively exact objective convergence, cap-volume convergence,
and full closed-fiber coverage in the realized limit. Unbounded integer
coefficients are not replaced by a vertical limiting cap.

The separate inball integral and the example with unit full ambient
normals both have the correct normalization and constants. The latter
retains a positive cap budget while its normalized hinge tends to zero;
the limiting vertical support plane acquires whole-fiber boundary mass.

For the fixed-normal stress, clipping unused thresholds to B_i must
precede selection of the coverage certificates. This was made explicit
after the audit. The remaining problem is a convex differentiable
minimization over a compact polyhedron. Its KKT signs give
c_i+kappa_i=sum_z eta_z lambda_zi, and upper-bound multipliers vanish
because at b_i=B_i both cap mass and lower-bound multiplier vanish.
The supporting-fiber resultants U_z cannot be dropped.

For the joint system I checked the finite-dimensional separation argument,
including the simplex coordinate inequalities. Allowing lambda_z to vary
is essential: their stationarity makes the SAME exposed point chosen in
the support gradient a true contact of every positively weighted cap.
The section data use the same effective trace for mass and all moments.
The unrestricted offset and integer-normal equations have the displayed
signs. Dotting the continuous equation with its unit normal gives
sigma_i=-alpha_0 Psi_i: the cap term contributes alpha_0 Psi_i, and
the remaining terms cancel by the mass, integer moment, section, and
contact equations. The system correctly permits alpha_0=0. It is not
a normalized joint KKT theorem without an additional qualification.

## 2. Common moment-body bridge and product calibration

Sources: `candidate b4c3b9c6a52059d2`,
`candidate a5428a02cd85fb48`, and
`candidate 0e807db2bba0c137`.

The support dual of the base-balanced moment body has a compact attained
primal. Strict separation from a point vertically above its optimal
constraint section proves dual equality without assuming dual attainment.
Its maximum feasible mass is at least the marginal closed-halfspace
capacity by the exact hinge tail integral. The regular Hessian is the
Schur complement of the integer-base-and-mass section matrix; all rank
and differentiability assumptions are explicit. The exact product gap
between this support and the separately optimized integrated tail is
1/24. Those two quantities cannot be identified.

The cover minimax certificate supplies a common convex combination of
normals even when its resultant is nonzero. The support dual then gives
the stated hinge bound with the full supporting-fiber term. An inball
of the common moment body gives the additional positive radius term.
The separate positive-inradius note constructs such a ball for every
mass strictly below the attained maximum, using actual dominated sources.

For the product calibration, equality in a simplex centroid cap forces
a canonical vertex cap. The independently proved multi-vertex gap
handles vertex-boundary coincidences. At each binary fiber centroid,
all d+1 canonical types are needed to cover a neighborhood, and one
cap cannot serve two fiber centroids at the given mass budget. The
specified total cap count therefore forces exactly those local cuts.
Their hinge integral is v H_j d gamma_d/(d+1)^2, giving the displayed
total M d gamma_d sum_j H_j/(d+1)^2. The globally affine binary-vertex
penalty realizes these cuts with finite integer tilts. In the regular
case all H_j=(d+1)r, so the total is M d r gamma_d.

## 3. Three-quarter source bound

Source: `candidate 6b83c9ea944bc6c0`.

The sharp scalar domain has the same necessity and attained two-band
simplex realization as the earlier fixed-mass density result, with
objective s+r. The substitutions U=1/s, E=r/s, Q=(s+alpha-r)/s transform
its constraint into phi(U)+2phi(Q)+2phi(E)>=2/(d+1).
Applying the three Fenchel inequalities with coefficients
tau, tau/2, -tau h/2 gives exactly tau(U+Q-hE). The displayed
dimensional inequality then implies the required source bound.

I checked the recovery algebra and the analytic estimates for d>=20,
and ran `supporting computation verify_fixed_mass_midpoint_three_quarter.py` successfully.
The finite d=1,...,19 checks have explicit integer certificates; the
remaining dimensions use a uniform proved estimate, with positive gap
1/120+14/(120d). No finite computational check substitutes for that
uniform argument.

The initial comparison sentence had placed the equality of the old
and new bounds at alpha=1/2. It has been corrected to alpha=1: the
new three-quarter bound dominates the older source bound throughout
0<=alpha<=1. The theorem itself and its proof were unaffected.

The hollow-double-triangle corollary uses a largest midpoint fiber B
and equal full endpoint masses a. The dominated midpoint coupling has
mass a and a deterministic centroid. Every ambient cap containing that
middle point pays at least the actual source cost, and the total mass
of the six fibers is at most 3(a+|B|). This proves the stated restricted
corollary. No unequal-vertex or arbitrary-projection conclusion follows.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
